name: Taroudant
hero_subtitle: The Little Marrakech of the Souss: intact ochre ramparts, unhurried souks, and the valley between the High Atlas and the Anti-Atlas.

overview.title: Welcome to the Little Marrakech of the Souss
overview.p1: Taroudant is often called the Little Marrakech — or la petite Marrakech — for its continuous 7.5 km of 16th-century ochre ramparts and its living medina. Framed by the High Atlas to the north and the Anti-Atlas to the south, this Souss Valley market town offers the atmosphere of a historic walled city without the intensity of larger tourist hubs.
overview.p2: Whether you circle the ramparts by calèche at sunset, bargain for Berber silver and argan products in the Arab and Amazigh souks, linger on Place Assarag, or day-trip to the palm oasis of Tiout, Taroudant rewards travellers who want authentic southern Morocco. Plan two to three days for the medina, the kasbah, local riads and the surrounding valley.

places.title: Places not to miss in Taroudant
places.subtitle: Ramparts, Place Assarag, Berber and Arab souks, the kasbah and quiet corners of the Little Marrakech.

assarag.title: Place Assarag
assarag.desc: The social heart of Taroudant: cafés, people-watching and the gateway to both souks.

remparts.title: The Ramparts
remparts.desc: 7.5 km of intact 16th-century adobe walls with 130 towers and monumental gates.

souks.title: Arab & Berber Souks
souks.desc: Relaxed markets for silver jewellery, leather, spices, produce and everyday life.

kasbah.title: The Kasbah
kasbah.desc: Former royal quarter in the north-east of the medina, with quieter lanes and square towers.

claudio.title: Palais Claudio Bravo
claudio.desc: Former home of the Chilean painter, now a palace-museum with gardens and citrus trees.

tannerie.title: Tanneries near Bab Targhount
tannerie.desc: Traditional leather workshops near Bab Targhount where sheep, goat and camel skins are still processed by hand.

bab_kasbah.title: Bab el-Kasbah
bab_kasbah.desc: The most ornate fortified gate of the ramparts, with views over the walls and the valley.

talmoklate.title: Place Talmoklate
talmoklate.desc: Secondary square linking the souks, with cafés and everyday market life in the medina.

tiout.title: Tiout Oasis
tiout.desc: Palm grove oasis about 30 minutes south-east, with a hilltop kasbah and quiet village paths.

argan.title: Argan cooperatives
argan.desc: Women’s cooperatives producing culinary and cosmetic argan oil near the city.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-day itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: A balanced plan to see the highlights of the Little Marrakech without rushing.

day1.title: Medina & walls
day1.desc: Explore Place Assarag, wander the souks, and tour the ramparts.

day2.title: Kasbah & crafts
day2.desc: Visit the kasbah, Bab el-Kasbah, and the Claudio Bravo palace or the tanneries.

day3.title: Oasis or free time
day3.desc: Head to Tiout oasis or argan cooperatives, or relax in your riad.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Start at Place Assarag for coffee and orientation, then walk or take a calèche along a stretch of the ramparts while the light is soft.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Wander both markets without a rigid plan. Look for silver, leather and spices; the pace is unhurried.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Return to the ramparts for the golden hour, then dinner in a riad or a simple restaurant near the square.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Explore the quieter kasbah quarter and the monumental Bab el-Kasbah gate; climb where allowed for views.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Reserve a visit to the Claudio Bravo palace-museum, or watch traditional tanning near Bab Targhount.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Book a table in a medina riad for home-style Moroccan cooking away from the busiest lanes.
detailed_itinerary.day3_m: Morning — Tiout Oasis or free time
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Leave early for Tiout oasis, the Anti-Atlas foothills, or Taliouine if booked. Otherwise stay in town for hammam and argan cooperatives.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: On the way back, stop at a women’s argan cooperative if you have not already; otherwise revisit favourite souk alleys.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Mint tea on a rooftop and an early night if you leave for Agadir or the Atlas the next morning.

transport.title: Getting around
transport.desc: The medina is compact and best explored on foot. For the full ramparts circuit, hire a calèche and agree the price before you start. Petit taxis serve the town; always ask for the meter.

bargain.title: Souk bargaining
bargain.desc: Shopping is calmer than in larger tourist cities. Start around half the asking price, stay friendly, and walk away if needed — vendors here serve local trade as much as visitors.

water.title: Stay hydrated
water.desc: Summers in the Souss Valley are hot. Drink bottled water, seek shade in the souks at midday, and save longer walks on the ramparts for morning or late afternoon.

daytrips.title: Best day trips from Taroudant
daytrips.subtitle: Rent a car, book a driver, or join a small group to reach these landscapes in a single day.

tiout.title: Tiout Oasis
tiout.desc: Palm groves, a hilltop kasbah and quiet village life about 30 minutes south-east.

antiatlas.title: Anti-Atlas foothills
antiatlas.desc: Berber villages, argan forests and rugged red-earth landscapes within easy reach.

taliouine.title: Taliouine saffron
taliouine.desc: Morocco’s saffron heartland east of Taroudant, with cooperatives and mountain views.

agadir.title: Agadir coast
agadir.desc: Atlantic beaches and the modern city about 1–1.5 hours west on the N10.

q1.question: How many days should I spend in Taroudant?
q1.answer: Two to three days is ideal for the Little Marrakech: one for the medina, walls and souks, one for the kasbah and a museum or cooperative, and optionally a day for Tiout oasis or the Anti-Atlas.

q2.question: Is Taroudant safe for tourists?
q2.answer: Yes. Taroudant is a quieter market town with a strong local character. Use the same common-sense precautions as in any medina: keep valuables secure and agree taxi fares in advance if the meter is not used.

q3.question: What currency is used and can I pay by card?
q3.answer: Morocco uses the dirham (MAD). Cards are accepted in many hotels and some restaurants; keep cash for the souks, calèches, petit taxis and small vendors.

q4.question: How do I get from Agadir airport to Taroudant?
q4.answer: Agadir Al Massira (AGA) is about 60–80 km west (roughly 1–1.5 hours by road). Private transfers, shared grands taxis and buses serve the route; book a transfer in advance if you arrive late.
